newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche - Horlick probe focus to stay in London.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche - Horlick probe focus to stay in London.

text.p: The focus of investigations into the departure of former top MGAM fund manager Nicola Horlick will remain in London, one of the senior Deutsche Bank AG officials who met her on Friday said on Monday.
"We did not take the initiative to bring the talks to Frankfurt, that came from Ms Horlick herself," the official, a company lawyer who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.

"We still consider it appropriate that the focus of the investigations is in London. All the experts are there and we would not consider it appropriate to take matters into our hands," the official said.

Horlick was suspended from her newly acquired position as managing director of MGAM last Tuesday amid allegations she tried to take a team of colleagues with her to another bank. She resigned on Thursday, alleging constructive dismissal, and is seeking reinstatement or compensation.

The 35-year-old this weekend said she wanted further talks with the legal official and human resources official from Deutsche Bank with whom she held a two-hour meeting after a dramatic impromptu trip to Frankfurt to plead her case to the management board.
Although she failed to meet top executives at Deutsche, Horlick said she had been given a fair hearing.
However the Deutsche legal official said he had passed on a report on the meeting with Horlick to the authorities in London, including facts and his overall impression of Horlick.

While he himself would likely play "a certain role" in the investigation, he said Deutsche's London investment banking arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and its asset management unit Morgan Grenfell Asset Management would take the lead.

MGAM chief executive Robert Smith and DMG chief executive Michael Dobson were the leaders of the probe, he said, adding that interviews on the case with Horlick's erstwhile colleagues had been completed.
Horlick has repeatedly denied allegations she tried to lure staff from MGAM, saying her first preference is to get her old job back -- an option viewed as highly unlikely in the City.
